name: All In One Custom Login Page Styler – Secure & Fully Customize Your WordPress Login Page
author: Zia Imtiaz

sections.description:
All In One Custom Login Page Styler is the most powerful plugin for fully customizing and securing your WordPress login page. Tailor every element of the login page, add extra security features, and ensure seamless access for your users. This feature-rich plugin helps you personalize the login page with your branding and protects it with advanced security tools.

From customizing logos to limiting login attempts and blocking IPs, All In One Custom Login Page Styler offers everything you need to control access, boost security, and enhance the overall login experience on your WordPress site.

Key Features

1. Complete Login Customization

  • Custom Logo: Replace the default WordPress logo with your brand’s logo.
  • Background Customization: Add a custom background image or solid color that aligns with your site’s theme.
  • Form Styling: Modify the login form’s width, border, padding, and font styles for a fully personalized experience.
  • Button Styling: Custom login button color, hover effects, and radius for a consistent look.

2. Boost Login Security

  • Google reCAPTCHA Integration: Add Google reCAPTCHA to prevent bots from accessing your login page and launching brute-force attacks.
  • Limit Login Attempts: Protect your site from brute-force attacks by limiting login attempts from individual IPs.
  • IP & Region Blocking: Block suspicious IP addresses or entire regions from accessing your login page.
  • Force Logout: Log users out forcefully when needed, improving site security in case of an active threat.

3. Create Temporary Login URLs

Generate temporary login URLs that provide access for a limited time (default of 7 days). Great for granting temporary admin access to collaborators or clients without needing to share a password.

4. Track Login Activity with Login Logs

Monitor user login activity with comprehensive login logs:
– Last Login Time
– User IP Address
– User Role
– Location Tracking

You can also view failed login attempts and take action in case of suspicious activity.

5. Customize Login Redirection

  • Redirect users to a custom URL after login or logout.
  • Use Login Redirection to guide users to the appropriate dashboard, homepage, or any page you specify.

6. Customize Your Login URL

Change the default WordPress login URL (wp-login.php) to a custom URL for added security, preventing attackers from easily accessing the login page.

7. Add Custom Login Link to Navigation Menu

Quickly add a login link to your site’s navigation menu for easy access. Optionally, hide unnecessary menu items to streamline the login page.

8. Hide WordPress Default Login Elements

  • Remove the WordPress logo from the login page.
  • Hide the “Back to Blog” link and any unnecessary navigation links.
  • Remove the “Lost your password?” link for extra security.

9. Passwordless Login for Seamless Experience

Allow users to log in using a secure, one-time link that eliminates the need for passwords, enhancing both user experience and security.

10. Login Shortcode

Add login buttons directly into posts or pages with the Login Shortcode feature for easy access anywhere on your site.

How do I customize my login page?

Go to the Login Customization section in the plugin settings. Modify your login logo, background, form fields, and button styles.

How do I enable Google reCAPTCHA?

In the Security Settings, add your Site Key and Secret Key. Get these keys from Google reCAPTCHA.

How can I restrict login by IP or region?

Use the IP & Region Blocking section to add specific IPs or entire regions to block.

Can I track login attempts and activity?

Yes! View login logs in the Login Logs section. This includes login time, IP address, user role, and location, as well as failed login attempts.

How do I create temporary login URLs?

Go to the Temporary Login URLs settings, set the expiration time, and generate secure one-time login URLs.

How do I redirect users after login?

In the Login Redirection settings, specify the page URL where users should be redirected after login or logout.

Can I limit login attempts?

Yes, in the Limit Login Attempts settings, you can set a maximum number of login attempts before temporarily locking out an IP.

How do I force log out users?

In the Login Logs section, simply select a user and click on “Force Logout” to immediately log them out.

Version 7.1.1

  • New Feature: Added Google reCAPTCHA integration for added protection.
  • Enhancement: Improved IP & Region Blocking functionality.
  • Fixes: Enhanced login log tracking with more details (e.g., user role, location).
  • Security: Improved Limit Login Attempts for better brute-force protection.

Version 6.2.6

  • Bug fixes and performance improvements.
  • Added Google Fonts for custom font styling.
  • Enhanced background image handling for responsive designs.

Version 7.1.1

This update includes critical security enhancements, including Google reCAPTCHA, IP/region blocking, and login attempt limits. It’s highly recommended to upgrade to ensure your login page is protected with the latest features and improvements.

Social Proof & Call to Action

Don’t just take our word for it—Thousands of users trust All In One Custom Login Page Styler to secure and style their WordPress login pages. If you find the plugin helpful, please leave a rating and review to help others discover it!

Why Choose All In One Custom Login Page Styler?

  • Complete Control: Customize your login page and secure it according to your needs.
  • Robust Security: With Google reCAPTCHA, IP blocking, and login limits, your site stays safe.
  • User-Friendly: Designed with non-technical users in mind, making it easy to use right out of the box.

Final Words

All In One Custom Login Page Styler isn’t just about looks—it’s about securing your site while offering the best user experience. Try it today to create a login page that’s as stylish as it is secure!
sections.installation:
1. Upload the Plugin: Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory or install directly via the WordPress admin panel.
  2. Activate the Plugin: Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Configure the Plugin: Go to Settings > Login Customization to modify the design, security settings, and login options.
